scope_note: Covers the leading U.S. commodity resins and important engineering/thermoset families. Commercial formulations contain variable additives and blends; the catalog is not exhaustive at formulation level.

resins.name: polypropylene
resins.replacement_priority: high for unnecessary single-use packaging and textiles; low until validated for critical medical and durable parts
resins.health_entity_note: Finished PP, propylene monomer, additives, manufacturing emissions, and PP particles require separate evidence.

resins.name: high-density polyethylene
resins.replacement_priority: high for avoidable bottles and packaging through refill/reuse; case-specific for pipe, medical, and industrial containment
resins.health_entity_note: The polyethylene chain must not be conflated with PFAS formed by fluorinating some HDPE containers.

resins.name: linear low-density polyethylene
resins.replacement_priority: very high for avoidable films and secondary packaging; controlled reuse or recovery for transport and agricultural films
resins.health_entity_note: Primary concern is high leakage and fragmentation potential plus formulation-specific additives, not a demonstrated universal toxicity of bulk LLDPE.

resins.name: low-density polyethylene
resins.replacement_priority: very high for unnecessary single-use film; preserve function where contamination or moisture protection materially prevents larger losses
resins.health_entity_note: PE particles appear in emerging human observational research, but source, dose, and causality are unresolved.

resins.name: polyvinyl chloride
resins.replacement_priority: highest for flexible high-exposure uses with hazardous plasticizers and avoidable short-lived products; application-specific for long-life infrastructure
resins.health_entity_note: Vinyl chloride monomer is a known human carcinogen; flexible PVC may contain phthalates; combustion can form dioxins/furans. Those hazards are not identical to ordinary contact with every finished PVC article.

resins.name: polyethylene terephthalate
resins.replacement_priority: high for single-use beverage packaging through tap/refill/deposit systems and for microfiber shedding control; retain where food protection has net benefit
resins.health_entity_note: No dashboard claim treats PET resin, its catalysts, and PET particles as one toxicological entity.

resins.name: polystyrene and expanded polystyrene
resins.replacement_priority: very high for disposable foodservice and loose-fill packaging; case-specific for insulation because operational energy benefits matter
resins.health_entity_note: Styrene is reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen based mainly on occupational/animal evidence; this is not a direct risk estimate for a foam cup.

resins.name: polyurethane
resins.replacement_priority: high for uncured spray applications and avoidable foam; performance-based comparison for building insulation and durable products
resins.health_entity_note: Diisocyanates used to make PU can cause irritation and occupational sensitization/asthma; cured products and reactive application stages must be separated.

resins.name: ABS, styrene-acrylonitrile, and acrylic polymer families
resins.replacement_priority: durability, repair, take-back, and safer chemistry before material substitution
resins.health_entity_note: Acrylonitrile and styrene monomer hazards are important in production; they do not quantify exposure from a finished ABS housing.

resins.name: polycarbonate and epoxy resin families
resins.replacement_priority: prioritize BPA-free/high-exposure food-contact and infant applications; retain critical safety functions pending validated substitutes
resins.health_entity_note: EPA notes endocrine-disruption concern for BPA, while FDA's dated page states approved food-contact uses were safe at then-assessed levels; show both positions and dates.

resins.name: polyamides including nylon 6 and nylon 6,6
resins.replacement_priority: reduce microfiber and fishing-gear loss, extend product life, and use take-back/recycling; compare natural fibers for land and water impacts
resins.health_entity_note: No universal resin-specific ingestion effect is established; particle shape, size, additives, and co-pollutants control evidence quality.

resins.name: fluoropolymers including PTFE and related PFAS polymers
resins.replacement_priority: phase out nonessential uses and processing aids with hazardous releases; essential-use analysis for safety-critical functions
resins.health_entity_note: Polymer PFAS, nonpolymer PFAS processing aids, residuals, emissions, and degradation products must not be collapsed into one exposure metric.
